name: Zimbabwe

facts.languages: Chibarwe, English, Kalanga, Khoisan, Ndau, Northern Ndebele, Chewa, Shona, Sotho, Tonga, Tswana, Tsonga, Venda, Xhosa, Zimbabwean Sign Language
facts.currency: Botswana pula, Chinese yuan, Euro, British pound, Indian rupee, Japanese yen, United States dollar, South African rand, Zimbabwean bonds

snapshot: Emmerson Mnangagwa signed a constitutional change in 2026 keeping him in office until 2030, two years beyond his term, as ZANU-PF eyes even longer.
culture: The stone city of Great Zimbabwe, built from the 11th century, gave the country its name. Shona and Ndebele are the largest languages, and mbira music, played on a thumb piano at spiritual ceremonies, is central to Shona culture. Chimurenga music, voiced by Thomas Mapfumo, carried the liberation struggle and later criticism of the government.
society: Zimbabwe has rich deposits of lithium, platinum and gold, but hyperinflation, currency collapses and land seizures have devastated the economy since 2000. Millions have emigrated, mostly to South Africa and Britain. A new gold-backed currency, the ZiG, launched in 2024. Opposition activists face arrest.
baseline: Mnangagwa took over after the 2017 military coup against Robert Mugabe. ZANU-PF pushed through a bill in mid-2026 to extend presidential and parliamentary terms, keeping him in office until 2030, despite objections that the constitution requires a referendum for such a change. Some in the party have since floated keeping him until 2037. War veterans and Vice President Constantino Chiwenga's allies have opposed the move.
